reviews.text: For a certain kind of mood, one filled with patience, forgiveness and the need to pass a few hours of time, The Lost City might almost be what the doctor ordered.
reviews.author: Pradeep Menon

reviews.text: The Lost City is the perfect palate cleanser for those who are looking for a fresh twist on the comedy genre.
reviews.author: Christian Eulinberg

reviews.text: Laughing, smiling, & losing my shit! Hands down one of the best comedies I’ve seen in awhile. I need more Channing Tatum & Sandra Bullock now! + Brad Pitt was amazing! This is the perfect Adventure film for all!
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Despite billing itself as a return to the entertaining adventure-romance movies of the ’80s (it’s impossible not to think of Romancing the Stone), The Lost City was afraid to lose itself in eccentricity.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: The Lost City is one of this year's surprises, managing to vary the well-known formulas of the genre in a creative, fun manner (...) a thematically rich ending compensates for any cliches. Definitely, a family viewing party recommendation.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: The Lost City is every bit the romantic adventure we didn’t know we needed and then some. It’s fun and hilarious, and its on-the-nose praise of the romance genre is something we’ll never tire of exploring.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum get blindsided by a wonky and aimless script better suited for the balls-to-the-wall performances of its side characters.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock’s return to light-hearted comedy is welcome. While not to be taken too seriously the film does throw in a few heartfelt moments.
reviews.author: Stacey Yvonne

reviews.text: Ultimately, the The Lost City is relatively hollow with a somewhat uncharacteristic denouement that connects back to Bullock’s late husband and her inability to let him go.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: ...the breezy chemistry with Sandra Bullock renders this a painless hijinx...
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The Lost City is at its best when it is light and silly, smoothing over some of the rougher edges where its jokes don't always land.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: The Lost City is a terrific throwback to studio romcoms of the 90s and 00s, with two true-blue movie star performances from Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: A story about the vicarious pleasures of romance fiction, and about the folly of either dismissing them as stupid or of taking them too seriously … The obviousness of the genre machinery isn’t really a flaw – it’s part of the fun.
reviews.author: Mel Campbell

reviews.text: [Channing Tatum's] energetic and eager to please — virtues he shares with the film.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: The sort of bubbly, unchallenging studio plaything that some of us may receive gratefully in these harrowed times.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Bullock is a solid anchor, Radcliffe gets a couple of humorous lines, and Tatum does his best. But it’s Pitt who steals the show. So much so that the drop-off is pretty significant whenever he’s not on screen.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: A word comes to mind that isn’t often used when describing movies lately. Thinking, thinking … oh, right! The word is “fun.” “The Lost City” is fun.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: An unofficial remake of 'Romancing the Stone' with a big movie star cameo.  Dull, obvious and very familiar with a script that just pokes along.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: There are five writers sharing screenplay credit, but for me the writing of Bullock's character was the weakest element.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: The breezy pace is appreciated, but in two years, viewers won't recall any discernible differences between this, Uncharted, and Jungle Cruise.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: ...coasts along on the charisma and chemistry of its stars.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Whilst its stars are all perfectly cast, including a wonderfully camp villain turn from Daniel Radcliffe, as well as Brad Pitt stealing the show in his brief supporting role, it doesn’t quite thread the needle.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: .... a fairly breezy comedy with some fun stunt sequences that play to the strengths of the cast ...
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: It lacks the grandeur and muscle that went into the old rom-com adventures, but it makes up for it in star power and in just being so agreeable. Channing Tatum really is one of the funniest people on Earth.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: To sum it all up, “The Lost City” is a fun way to usher in the spring movie season.
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Hollywood should still make thoroughly predictable yet still well-executed and gleaming-enough fare like this, and more often.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: ...erratic yet mostly watchable...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: It's impossible to hold a grudge against it, because at its core, it's sincere. We can't judge it by its cover. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: The comedy chemistry between Bullock and Tatum steadily improves throughout the picture, as does its writing and direction.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Its adventure comedy is a tremendous nonsense and it only gives me a feeling of apathy when I see the stiff characters of Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum lost in the jungle of clichés. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Breezy, romantic and funny...
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: It's never truly egregious, but The Lost City is devoid of passion or strong character work - neither romantic nor truly comedic. It’s hard to muster up much of a response to the aggressively underwhelming hijinks at work here beyond a shrug.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Formula done right is one reason the lightweight romantic romp, The Lost City, works. Another is the unassuming, easy-going chemistry between its two leads, Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Recaptures that Hollywood tradition in the best way, with a leading duo that overflows with charisma and beauty. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: Why reinvent [the genre] when the livelong recipe continues to work with minimal variations? [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text:
Star power and chemistry prove to be the only way to uplift a mediocre script to the end.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: The Lost City is a cute romantic comedy that brings the adult humor and fun, but it shows too many of the good parts in the trailers. Radcliffe, however, completely steals the show.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: …Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum strike sparks, there’s a fun supporting cast, some gags and cameos, and a good time is on offer; what’s not to like?
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Find 'The Lost City' for romantic adventure.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: It's best to just sit back, devour some popcorn, and let this easy-going flick roll right through you.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: A little adventure over here, a bit of romance over there, and a pinch of legend cooked to the slow fire of absurd comedy… Such is the recipe... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ezequiel Boetti

reviews.text: It's easy to take the slick, surface-level, time-tested pleasures of "The Lost City" for granted, but it's not easy to make grand throwback adventure flicks work this well.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: If you want to laugh, be scared and thrilled with a blockbuster that doesn't take itself too seriously, it's certainly worth seeing on the big screen. It serves as a respite between so many new instalments of famous franchises. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: "The Lost City" earns its satisfying final moments. It's a hilarious and action-packed film that's maybe ten minutes too long, sure. But more importantly, it's a heartwarming and creative romance between two of Hollywood's most lovable movie stars.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: Exactly the kind of mid-sized movie we often lament the modern absence of, The Lost City is a surprisingly awesome throwback.
reviews.author: Dominic Corry

reviews.text: We need more comedy in this world, and what better way to achieve that than through viewing the Queen of Comedy, Sandra Bullock, or "Miss Congeniality" while munching on popcorn in a movie theater, and yes, Channing Tatum and Brad Pitt are always a plus.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: A screwball comedy that's as silly as hell.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The Lost City is front-loaded with a few funnies most of which you’ve already seen in the trailer before what's left of the comedy is stretched thinly across the rest of the inanity.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Riotously funny, supremely silly and with star power in spades, The Lost City is a real gem of an action comedy.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: The Lost City is a warm, big-hearted treat, a delight from start to finish, a glorious throwback to simpler times, simpler stories and shameless, brazen high adventure.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: The Lost City is exactly the kind of throwback rom-com adventure that is elevated from fine to riotous thanks to the presence of Sandra Bullock
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: This is a formulaic, crowd-pleasing popcorn movie, which is sometimes exactly what many of us yearn for.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: Surprisingly tepid...the film has a prolonged middle section in which the directors try hard as heck to generate comic and romantic sparks between Bullock and Tatum. It's way too forced...Still, as a holiday time-killer you could do worse.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: "The Lost City" isnt a big movie, even with its big stars. Its out to provide audiences with an undemanding good time. Its a modest goal, but its one the movie reaches.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: There is something so refreshing in watching true movie stars give their bigscreen charisma room to breathe
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: It is nice to once again see that 2022 is the year of the rom-com and this film is another one that nails the genre and presents itself to the audience as a fun time at the movies.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: Ultimately there is not much to recommend The Lost City beyond a degree of unpretentious good nature, plus the appeal of its stars. But depending on your fondness for Bullock and Tatum, that may be enough to make you feel you haven’t been robbed.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: These are two charming actors who play off each other with manic enthusiasm. Alas, the screenplay is woefully short on screwball energy.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock is on terrific form in this rollicking romcom.
reviews.author: Veronica Lee

reviews.text: The Lost City gives us the escapist entertainment we need right now.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A romantic comedy that signals a return to form for a beloved genre.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum have an easy, winning chemistry... but the script is uneven, working too hard too often for the laughs.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Brad Pitt’s hilarious cameo, Daniel Radcliffe’s winking evilness and Da’Vine Joy Randolph’s antics compensate for the lazy patches of writing and the mid-narrative slump in mood.
reviews.author: Scroll Staff

reviews.text: The Lost City, for the most part, finds that sweet spot between goofy and sincere, especially during the scenes where Tatum’s Alan tries to match up to the mercenary hired to rescue Loretta, played by none other than Brad Pitt.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: It’s fun for the most part, borrowing shamelessly from Indiana Jones movies and Romancing The Stone. And Brad Pitt makes a hilarious cameo.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The Lost City is far too derivative for its own good and is rarely as clever as it thinks it is. However, Bullock’s comic chops are impeccable as ever,
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: What follows is a hilarious screwball adventure-comedy that will evoke memories for certain generations of both Romancing the Stone (especially with its use of ‘80s hits like Spandau Ballet’s True and Pat Benatar’s Shadows of the Night) and Nim’s Island.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: The Lost City proves just how much extra mileage you can get from a well-worn premise if you get the casting right.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Director siblings Aaron and Adam Nee are the missing link between the Farrelly brothers and Joel and Ethan Coen. This is the third film they’ve made together and it’s a grubby little gem.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum make a sweet and spiky couple in this likeable caper. It’s never going to challenge The African Queen for quality, but it offers  a consistently good time.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum go troppo. Hee-hum.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: 'The Lost City' isn't what you want it to be, but it's trying to be. It's not 'Romancing The Stone', but then again, what is?
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: While 'The Lost City' doesn't reinvent the rom-com action-adventure formula, it's happy to sit within the conventions of this classic genre and serve precisely what you came for.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: The movie proves front-loaded; the jokes thin out. But that first half is a riot, screwball set to a delightfully skewed rhythm, Bullock the sequinned straight man to Tatum’s neurotic himbo.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A sexy, smart, self-aware studio comedy with an original premise and a bona fide A-list cast that gets by on more than pre-existing brand awareness.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: This is all amiable enough, with the all-important dimension of laughs: Tatum and Bullock showing that they are smart enough to know how silly it is, and that they know that we know that they know.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A funny rom-com adventure, elevated by its irresistible leads.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: ‘The Lost City’ is a pretty serviceable action-adventure comedy with a lot of star power and some breathtaking visuals.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: Full of personality and plenty of twists and turns to keep the predictable action skipping along, The Lost City is daft and delightful in equal measure; the perfect cinematic indulgence.
reviews.author: Emily Breen

reviews.text: In terms of pure fun, this might just be one of the most joyous cinema experiences of the year so far.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: The Lost City is what could be described as knowingly dated: it’s a film designed to make you regret they don’t make ’em like this any more, even when “this” means escapist Hollywood fluff.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Star power swings to the rescue of a breezy romantic adventure that sticks to charted territory.
reviews.author: Matthew Leyland

reviews.text: Old fashioned in its approach, The Lost City is a warm and satisfying comedy for those who want something undemanding from their cinema visit.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: I enjoyed this movie more than I thought I would. I thought I knew about how it would go, but there were a couple of surprises, and the movie was written better than I thought it would be, with a lot of funny references to other adventure movies.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: The lumbering The Lost City hasnt a whit of cleverness about which to care.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Brad Pitt, who shows up in an extended 10-odd minute cameo is the only saving grace of this dumpster fire of a film.
reviews.author: Shikhar Verma

reviews.text: This isn't a perfect film, but hopefully those involved with making The Lost City believe in that message because they have nothing to be embarrassed about. This movie will make an awful lot of people happy.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: Good talent doing something we've seen done before, and not doing it all that well.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: The Lost City is a reminder of Hollywood offerings past, a throwback movie experience that, while slight, is a heck of a lot of fun. At the risk of sounding curmudgeonly, they don't often make 'em like this anymore. One might even call it ... a lost art.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: Rather than explore new directions, it follows clearly marked footsteps of Romancing the Stone — which in turn drew from Indiana Jones. Like those movies, The Lost City provides pleasant escapism.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: It's a delightful romp that brings back the long-lost adventure comedies of the good old days but with a new perspective.
reviews.author: Marriska Fernandes

reviews.text: An overall breezy fun adventure-comedy backed by Brad Pitt's scene-stealing cameo as well as Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum's amusing star power.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Adam and Aaron Nees throwback romp The Lost City serves as a healthy reminder that not all playful, high-concept comedies have to exist solely for the streaming services.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The Lost City is a featherweight comedy that resists larger meaning. But it speaks to our cultural moment, wherein the present and future look so awful that we can only find pleasure by turning to the past.
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: What The Lost City gets right is casting leads capable of being charming and funny with equal aplomb.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: A warmed-over, mediocre adventure romance that is reckless with its promising premise and charismatic cast.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The adventure is action-packed, full of tender romance between hot actors, and one of the funniest films youll see in theaters this year. In fact, its one of the funniest rom-coms youll have seen in years.
reviews.author: Mey Rude

reviews.text: Despite the best efforts of its talented cast, the film cannot sustain the momentum of its promising start and meanders along at a sluggish clip.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: There wasn't much chemistry between Bullock and Tatum - until they danced. If the whole movie had had that much appeal it would have been much better.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: As great an example as you'll find in these fallow days of a pure-bred Movie Star Picture.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Mildly enchanting but mostly forgettable, this derivative jungle adventure features some charismatic performances and a breezy silliness without any substance beneath its broad surface laughs to hold it together.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text:
Brad Pitt is in it for a brief amount of time and practically steals the movie....
I laughed out loud. Have fun. Why not? It's been a very long, dreary winter and this is a breath of fresh air.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: A stellar sense of humor and fresh writing leads to lots of laughs and a romantic adventure that turns out to be a diamond in the rough.
reviews.author: Katarina Docalovich

reviews.text: Amusing escapist adventure - with revelatory post-credits scenes.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Most importantly, it will make you happy. What more could we ask for as theaters begin to ramp up for the summer movie season.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: Its all very unimaginative, and the entertaining qualities they claimed easily fall to pieces.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: It works because of the chemistry between Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: The Lost City finally fills in the very specific movie gap that The Mummy left behind.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: For an amusing almost-two hours, The Lost City will entertain.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: It's an enjoyable mix of nutty gags, bonkers action and cute interaction, and it even grapples with a few solid themes along the way.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Even Brad Pitt's hilarious ex-Navy SEAL can't save Bullock's anemic action comedy...
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: I squirm and moan my way through stinkers all the time, but I can’t actually remember the last time I saw a submental farce this witless, boring and stupid.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Though it relies on premise more than plot, The Lost City stands tall among its rival predators in the catalog of action comedies.
reviews.author: Ray Gill Jr.

reviews.text: Flaws be damned: Aaron Nee and Adam Nee's "The Lost City" is the perfect blend of silly-stupid with wide appeal that a weary movie-going audience needs right now.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: If youre looking for a good time and plenty of laughs, youll enjoy this charming comedy. Bullock and Tatum have great chemistry.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: The Lost City is what it says on the tin, and we appreciate its honesty. This movie isn't going to change anyone's life, but it's a good time, and there is some hidden depth for people looking for the emotional connection between the artist and their art.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: It's not really all that great, but I enjoyed it.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Its the Bullock & Tatum show, which is exactly what the doctor ordered.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: ...a gloriously silly movie that owes a lot to the 1984 hit Romancing The Stone.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: It’s a pity, because The Lost City could’ve easily been the movie that reminds studios why we need to take rom-coms back to the big screen. And maybe make audiences fall in love with this genre all over again.
reviews.author: Will Ashton

reviews.text: The Lost City had the potential to tell a moving story and instead opted to play it safe.
reviews.author: Mark Goodyear

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum have chemistry plus Radcliffe doesn't overplay the villain.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: Not since Muhammad Ali and George Foreman have heavyweights been this entertaining in the jungle.
reviews.author: Whelan Barzey

reviews.text: The Lost City hits cinemas like a charming throwback to the star-driven Hollywood comedies of the late 1990s and early 2000s: driven by star power, a high concept premise, and a fairly visible debt to older, more accomplished movies.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The Lost City is a funny and warm romantic comedy, even if its not original in any way at all. The leads make it worth it.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: While some glints of chemistry allow for this to scrape along to the convenient finale, a lack of anything substantial, whether it be characterization or comedic range, ultimately makes The Lost City feel like its longevity will be, well, lost.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: Brad Pitt  the only one having some fun  of course is the first to exit, & we're left with no-chemistry Bullock and Tatum, shirts-off jokes & Radcliffe painfully portraying a villain as if he's never seen a Bond film (the Rami Malik School). Lifeless!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: It’s bright, both visually and atmospherically. It’s an original story, told by filmmakers who get what kind of movie this is.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It is nothing more than Romancing the Stone through a repackaged studio lens that romances the rehash.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: The only reason Im willing to give this film something of a halfhearted recommendation is based solely on the undeniably magnetic chemistry generated by Bullock and Tatum.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: The Lost City has to be one of the best movies of 2022. Its hilarious, super quotable, and has a rock solid cast.
reviews.author: Kristen Maldonado

reviews.text: The Lost City refreshingly harkens to a time when movie stars embraced their charismatic personas.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: A harmless and mildly engaging, yet forgettable diversion. The supporting characters are more interesting and funny than the main cast.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: A microwave burrito of a movie: You’ll eat it while wondering why.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: The Lost City is a passable diversion.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The Lost City is fairly predictable and conventional, but it's elevated by a good performance by Sandra Bullock and Bullock and Channing Tatum's oddly good chemistry as a romantic pairing.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: THE LOST CITY in no way reinvents the wheel in this action-adventure comedy but Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum are so much fun to watch on screen with their goofy antics.  Adding Brad Pitt in the mix makes for some of the funniest moments.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: The Lost City is a smoothly engineered crowd-pleaser with a few twists, lots of clever quips, and a wholly predictable structure.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: As it is, despite the film being perfectly competent, I dont recommend seeing it. Because you already have. Many times.
reviews.author: Tyler Smith

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum romance the stone  in Raiders of the Lost City, I mean, The Lost City.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It's not a spectacular send-off, and Bullock will doubtless be back in the spotlight at some point. But whether it means to or not, The Lost City sends her lovelorn movie-star persona off into the sunset.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: They built this "City" on a flimsy foundation.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Action, comedy, and romance are the hallmarks of many movies. The Lost City serves up generous amounts of each of these  ingredients yet still feels no more than adequate.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: It's a nice, throwaway date-night movie. Don't think too much about it.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Like a Sprinkles red velvet cupcake, you don't want to make a steady diet of it, but it's a fabulous treat occasionally, especially when the outside world is so gloomy, it brightens the inside world with glorious, gooey goodness, if only for a few hours.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: There is nothing original in Adam and Aaron Nees fresh take on stale popcorn like Romancing the Stone except for the charisma of its cast.  And theres plenty of zing and genuine fun to be had in the matchup of Bullock and Tatum...
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Our would-be heroes eventually fail upward into their inevitable reconciliation... dragging on to deliver a mercifully okay ending and an acceptable denouement, a sad hint of what shouldnt come from a sequel that has even less of a right to exist.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: The Lost City is a charming, albeit weightless, romantic comedy less concerned with its ridiculous plot and more centered on delivering entertaining characters.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Don’t get me wrong, the film has plenty of “didn’t see that coming” moments -- it’s just they’re front loaded.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It is all charming old-school humor, and it works.... Bullock and Tatum are game, and "The Lost City" is a crowd-pleaser
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Feels like the kind of breezy mid budget studio comedy the likes of which are very much an endangered species nowadays, and that makes it something that should be cherished and protected.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: A serviceable high-concept comedy with one incontrovertible truth: Patti Harrison should be in every movie.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: A ridiculous, fun-filled romp about an illusion behind an illusion.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: A romantic comedy adventure for those nostalgic about how these felt in days of yore, but who’d just as soon skip the less agreeable specifics – and who have a tolerance for hit-and-miss laughs.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: One of those high-concept ideas where the plot is ridiculous, but it doesnt matter because the movie gets every other element right.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Let us praise the genius of Sandra Bullocks gift for physical comedy.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum are very good, very charming movie stars, cognizant of their packaged personalities and front-facing strengths
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Half the gags land, if that, and the plot doesn’t even try to hold our interest. But Bullock and Tatum make a terrific team, bickering as nimbly as dueling jazz musicians in a virtuoso duet, redeeming even lines that have no right to be so charming.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: The chemistry between Bullock and Tatum makes The Lost City a fresh, remarkably funny take on a familiar story.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Entertaining from beginning to end, with lots of laughs, beautiful scenery, and a cast committed to delivering a great film.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: It's pretty dumb. Even so, it sort of works.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: "The Lost City" pops more often than it flounders with the charisma between Tatum and Bullock providing enough juice to overcome the film's many shortcomings.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Bullock, Tatum and an extended superstar cameo instigate a few laughs but, among other miscues, the tepid screenplay offers no infusion of 'Harry Potter'-like magic for an allegedly villainous turn by Daniel Radcliffe. (mini review)
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: It’s a decent setup as far as it goes, but that’s as far as it goes.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Is it better than Romancing the Stone? No, of course not. Though it's far better than Jewel of the Nile...which kind of makes this the Romancing sequel we deserved back then, but never got.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: City is amiable if uninspired, too loyal to rom-com conventions to really send them (or any other genre) up, rendering a ripe satirical opportunity never more than mildly humorous.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: It's no Romancing the Stone, but the stars work overtime to entertain, with Tatum a particular highlight.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: You can't Hail Mary your entire film by casting great personas and hoping that gets you through the entire production. That never works. It's essentially what the filmmakers of The Lost City have done, and it shows.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: You'll recognize the romantic comedy formula here but it's been so long since we've seen a movie of this ilk that "Lost City" feels fresh.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Sometimes it works — let’s say 12 percent of the time — and “The Lost City” can actually be deft and imaginative. Unfortunately, that leaves 88 percent which doesn’t.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Theres not much wrong with it, but it reaches for nothing. It sets a very modest goal and barely exceeds it.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The Lost City is a ridiculous and heartwarming package. While some innuendos prohibit it from being a family-friendly film for all, it's entertaining for most. The charming cast has great comedic chemistry.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: Trapped in the jungle with Tatum and Bullock? There are worse places to be.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Yes, it's about as formulaic as they come and there are few surprises. Yet, it all goes down so easily and agreeably that you simply can't put up much resistance when it comes to finding some parts or the entire offering to your liking.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: As a broadly goofy comedy featuring two enormously charismatic leads who are perfectly suited to each other, it scratches a particular itch very, very effectively.
reviews.author: Linda Holmes

reviews.text: Is it perfect? Absolutely not. Is it a good time from start to finish? Oh, hell yes.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Daniel Radcliffe may have ... delivered my favorite performance as the alternatingly goofy and menacing Abigail; the way he says coital reverie while discussing the tawdriness of Sages books made me laugh out loud.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The Lost City cruises for long stretches on the charm of its stars and the outlandish stunts of its adventure, but ultimately there are few jokes worth treasuring.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: No matter how preposterous the plot gets  and it gets very preposterous  watching the stars bounce off each other offers sufficient pleasure.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: This all-over-the-place, all-silly, all-star (Bullock, Tatum, Radcliffe, Pitt) throwback to 1980s escapismthink Romancing the Stoneradiates such a puppy-dog eagerness to please that you want to pet it instead of pointing out its faults.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Channing Tatum and Brad Pitt are two movie stars who often try to redirect attention to their peers. But theyre playing characters who, while on a rescue mission, compete against each other for that movie star glow. They make the pettiness beautiful.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text:
Lead duo chemistry? Yes. Entertaining? Yes.
But persistently funny? No. That is a mortal sin for movies that ask you not to take them seriously.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: With the effortlessly charming and talented cast doing most of the heavy lifting, The Lost City makes for a highly entertaining, joyful adventure.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: This romantic action adventure ... pulls its inspiration from Romancing the Stone (1984), but it injects enough originality to make the implausible film a treat for audiences weary of Hollywoods sequel-reboot cycle.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Bullock is always able to command our attention, and Tatum makes an excellent foil. If The Lost City never finds its way above middlebrow, at least it knows its place. Enjoy.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: A big dumb fun action-comedy, but everyone involved is aware of its own sheer goofiness and fully embraces it. It doesn't earn brownie points for originality, but the fun rapport of the cast elevates the so-so script.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: We need more films like "The Lost City" to break up the monotony of comic book films and awards movies.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: Mostly, the movie benefits from having Bullock back as a comic actress, one of the best in the biz. Sure, she can play serious roles exceedingly well, but Bullock is masterful at using her voice and body to hilarious effect.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: What I love about this movie is how much it pokes fun at its own genre. Its an adaptation of a romance novel, about a romance novel, written by a romance novelist, who hates romance novels.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: Its a modestly successful popcorn flick thanks to its likable leads and lighthearted screwball atmosphere.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: If you know in advance what you are getting yourself into and you dont expect too much, The Lost City is a fun way to spend a few hours.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Directors Aaron Nee and Adam Nee keep things moving so the various plot holes fly by without disrupting the popcorn pleasure of seeing Bullock get over her inhibitions and assumptions, Tatum dance, and Pitt be cool.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The movie itself is trying to excavate a long-lost genre: the big-budget action-adventure movie-star rom-com. It wants to be a modern Romancing the Stone so badly you can almost see the flop-sweat dripping down the screen.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: The Lost City could have been more of a throwaway studio flick. It was quite the opposite.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Like much of the romance genre, The Lost City has its problems, but its a surprisingly pleasant slice of entertainment.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: If the history of Hollywood will ever be written in hieroglyphics, future historians will see an engraving of Ms. Bullock tenaciously pulling off the musty old gag in which a heroine realizes her 5-inch heels can't keep up with her antics.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Breezy, silly, possibly quickly forgettable—but if you need to lose yourself for an hour or two, it could be just the thing.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Theres effortless chemistry between Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum, which is key to having a film like this work.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The poster made it look kind of fun, and lo and behold, it is.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: When did Hollywood decide that all globe-trotting adventures have to be extremely stupid?
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It doesn't reinvent the wheel in its subsequent genre, but THE LOST CITY's full embrace of its silly and fun vibe helps take its viewers on a ride.
reviews.author: Sarah Musnicky

reviews.text: Theres no brand to gravitate to or dopamine reward for recognizing things you grew up withjust charisma, comedy, and star power in spades.
reviews.author: Conor O'Donnell

reviews.text: A limp, laborious reminder of more enjoyable examples of the genre; even the effects are second-rate... meant to be dumb fun; unfortunately, it offers a lot of the first, but very little of the second.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The movie gives us the promises of a somewhat clever idea and some good-humored actors, and then, it simply and unfortunately hopes for the best.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: ...a movie that just barely works, powered by a star firing on all of her charismatic cylinders.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: The Lost City is like an underachieving student everyone knows can and should do better. Instead, its content to coast on the charisma of its two stars. While the hope is to find some (box office) treasure, its a chest full of untapped potential.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: The Lost City is a subtweet of contemporary Hollywood. Its also a capitulation.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: It doesn't rewrite the book on adventure-based rom-coms, but for a few hours in the jungle, one could find a lot worse.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: "The Lost City" adds up to a comedic effort that's not bad, exactly. It's just that when a movie is this close to being great, you wish it could've kept searching for treasure instead of settling for staying back at base camp.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: Its the essential likability that Sandra Bullock brings to her performance and the enjoyment of seeing Bullock and Tatum go at each other, verbally and physically, that makes the film fun. This isnt a groundbreaking comedy or action film...
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Maybe it was because I needed the kind of escapist light action-adventure fare The Lost City provides, but the movie made me laugh. A lot. Like when Beth reminds Loretta how to speak in front of the fans: No grumpy face, big words or academic talk.
reviews.author: Patricia Puentes

reviews.text: In a movie landscape dominated by superhero projects that are all somehow linked to each other, settling in to watch The Lost City feels almost like a novel experience.
reviews.author: Carly Lane

reviews.text: “The Lost City” isn’t a bad movie, and it’s sufficiently ridiculous for those seeking a gonzo escape with A-listers.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: A brief appearance by Brad Pitt as a resourceful adventurer is effective, while Bullock and Tatum are fine, which is an apt description of this popcorn flick you'll forget about by the time you get to your car.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: A relentlessly and eventually exhausting middle-ground effort that is made all the more frustrating because it is so very close to reaching the platonic ideal of shlock.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Not funny enough to be a comedy with some action and not action packed enough to be an action comedy, The Lost City is somewhere in the mushy middle.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Anyone who watches this motion picture and says they truly disliked it is probably telling a fib.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: This zesty zip of ripping rom-commery is a fun-filled frolic with a hilariously saucy, playfully risqué spin.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: For the most part, “The Lost City” delivers exactly what it promises: A couple of highly polished avatars quipping and hitting their marks while occasionally being upstaged by their second bananas.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Even gifts as prodigious as Bullock’s and Tatum’s can’t keep “The Lost City” afloat.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The Lost City's endearing characters, strong performances, and enthusiastic embrace of genre tropes elevate a by-the-numbers plot.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Only fans of the lightest, dopiest comedy could enjoy star’s hit-and-miss banter and muddled jungle courtship with Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum are screwball gold together. Neither are ever too vain for the bit, and she especially gets to show off her skills as a physical comedian.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: It lets its 2 stars shine with terrific chemistry, the adventure sizzles and most importantly it's laugh out loud funny
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Completely predictable on every level, The Lost City is saved by the considerable comedic talents of its starring cast members. It's breezy and lightweight entertainment that doesn't try to be anything else.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The Lost City is a middling adventure comedy that could've used a lot more of both genres. If this is to be Bullock's last starring role for a while, it's too bad it had to be in a film that doesn't live up to its - or her - potential.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Treasure hunting + adventure + comedy + romance seems like a formula for cinematic success, and, indeed, Paramount Pictures has struck gold here.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Filmmakers can’t depend on funny actors to go out there cold and bring back laughs. They have to be given funny things to do.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Star power and chemistry can still go a long way.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: You might swear you already saw this movie 20 years ago on TBS, but maybe that cozy conventionality is a selling point in uncertain times.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The Lost City isn’t terrible, just aggressively mediocre. It is the kind of movie you put on in the background after coming across it on TBS while you fold laundry on a Sunday afternoon.
reviews.author: Angelica Jade Bastién

reviews.text: The Lost City amounts to a predictable mix of comedy, romance and adventure, but its certainly an entertaining treasure worthy to be found.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Channing Tatum and Sandra Bullock have an amiable, infectious chemistry that helps paper over the movie’s predictability. Viewers may know where “The Lost City” is going at every turn but half the fun is getting there.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: You'd be better off watching "Romancing the Stone" again.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: This watered-down adventure displays considerable genericness; the screenplay needs inspiration and stimulation as desperately as the romance novelist.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The Lost City has the bad tang of squandered potential, misusing its massively appealing stars and failing the possibility of its premise.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: A return to rom-com form for one of our best and brightest stars of the genre. Bullocks still got it, and she wont soon let you forget it.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: You can't write this kind of movie. What is there to write except wisecracks and a MacGuffin plot? But like the best of its forebears, what makes The Lost City work is the chemistry of its leads.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum take hold of the material and turn it into an enchanted screwball.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: It will delight the masses. Its fun and entertaining for the entire family.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Theres no doubt that Bullock and Tatum make a great looking couple, and theres no denying their chemistry. The writing doesn't quite match up, however.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Falls into a pit of molasses once its electrifying extended cameo exits the story, sinking and sinking until one drowns in all the excess tropes
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The movie whiffs as far as doing anything creative or interesting with the development of its story, and regularly delivers the sense that there was a better version of the script that was drowned in rewrites.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum have an immediate, physical comedy chemistry that packs almost nonstop laughs, some of which come very close to bellyache inducing.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: The Lost City is a well-written, delightful movie sure to satisfy people looking for a great time at the movies.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: A lingering frustration hovers over the proceedings: The cast is so game, but the script is too inconsistent to deliver a steady stream of laughs.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: The Lost City is a wacky slapstick adventure loaded with saucy double entendres. Sandra Bullock, Channing Tatum, and a scene-stealing Brad Pitt are hilarious in a better than expected romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: The Lost City is a welcomed addition to the action rom-com sub-genre despite its flaws. A film that, if successful at the box office, may lend a hand in the studio's confidence in green-lighting future non-franchise big-budget blockbusters.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: Bullock and Tatum are entirely in their comedic zones when it comes to where they can really excel.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock is our reigning screwball queen and god help anyone who tries to take her crown away.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: “The Lost City” is a fun romp that is conscious of not overstaying its welcome with its run time — a seemingly rare quality these days — but it leaves you wanting both less and more.
reviews.author: KiMi Robinson

reviews.text: The Lost City is proof that star power and chemistry can only take a film with a mediocre script so far.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Nothing in Lost City would really hang together without its main pair, whose chemistry movies like this inevitably live or die on.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: This delightful Sandra Bullock/Channing Tatum flick evokes nostalgia for when films like this were Hollywood's bread-and-butter and adults could be trusted to show up for grown-up movies.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: Successfully does its job at offering escapist entertainment and quite a few chuckles as to not offend those not expecting more.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The Lost City is bland and messy whenever Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum arent on screen. Thankfully, their comedic banter is front and center for most of the film.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: A wildly entertaining riff on the adventureromance genre, thanks to the chemistry between Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Collier Jennings

reviews.text: Fool's Gold or Six Days Seven Nights failed much harder, so 'good enough' might be enough for The Lost City.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Its not the most original action-comedy ever made, but it does what it sets out to do; giving the audience a good time.
reviews.author: Sarah Ksiazek

reviews.text: Fun, nothing too much more and definitely nothing less, is exactly what the film delivers.
reviews.author: Kevin Fallon

reviews.text: The Lost City feels like a Sandra Bullock rom-com from 20 years ago, and she has instant chemistry with Channing Tatum.
reviews.author: Tiffany Kelly

reviews.text: For all the things you can otherwise accuse The Lost City of being  predictable, tension-free  smug isnt one of them. The movie is affectionate towards its protagonists, and we come to be as well.
reviews.author: David Lynch

reviews.text: The Lost City packs a lot of plot within its runtime, yet with Bullock and Tatum able to handle everything that is thrown at them.
reviews.author: Ryan McQuade

reviews.text: The Lost City is a film you can escape your troubles with for a couple of hours. Award-winning? Nope, but it is fun (and funny!)
reviews.author: Sarah Jane

reviews.text: Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum create a rhythm of movement and sound that causes their dynamite chemistry to leap off-screen and smack you in the face.
reviews.author: Valerie Complex

reviews.text: Movie stars, derring-do, laughter, heart, adventure. The Lost City brings it all together in a film seemingly plucked from that 80s heyday, garnished with a modern twist, and served up to movie theaters everywhere.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: [Tatum's] hunky character’s puppy-like devotion to Bullock’s dismissive damsel in distress serves the pic quite well, enlivening action that (after a winningly over-the-top kickoff) might otherwise grow too generic.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: “The Lost City” won’t be nominated for any Oscars, but it repeats what Spielberg and Lucas did for “Raiders of the Lost Ark,” mining a century-old genre for inspiration and polishing those tropes for a new generation.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Whenever The Lost City seems in danger of falling prey to other big-time star-studded adventures, particularly those calculated by Netflix, the obvious chemistry between Tatum and Bullock saves the day.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: The Lost City is a fun ride and a loving throwback to a certain kind of star-laden character-led adventure films Hollywood doesnt seem to have time for anymore.
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: It's pleasant, though it's unlikely to satisfy those thirsting for action and adventure.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

synopsis: Reclusive author Loretta Sage writes about exotic places in her popular adventure novels that feature a handsome cover model named Alan. While on tour promoting her new book with Alan, Loretta gets kidnapped by an eccentric billionaire who hopes she can lead him to an ancient city's lost treasure from her latest story. Determined to prove he can be a hero in real life and not just on the pages of her books, Alan sets off to rescue her.
